title: Iris and the Sky Bloom
markdown:
Iris, witch of the Whispering Peaks, hummed a tune that sounded like wind whistling through rocky passes. High above the treeline her home was a cozy clutter of dried herbs and unusual tools. Whisk, her always-alert stoat, twitched his whiskers, bright eyes following dust motes in a sunbeam. Mule paths, like forgotten ribbons, wound the mountainside where deep ravines carved ancient lines.

The mayor of Glimmerbrook had just rushed away, wringing his hands, a small ordinary grey stone clutched tight. “The Sparkle Stone has lost its shine. The Frost Festival is tomorrow. Only a Sky Bloom can rekindle it, and it blooms on the highest most perilous peak. You must use your dazzling magic.”

Iris traced a faded line on parchment. Whisk chittered from a dusty spellbook. “Ancient texts say the Sky Bloom likes a spot where mist kisses the bell tower at dawn. No thunderbolts. Clever timing and a good climb.” She tapped the map. “This old thing should show the way.”

It was a masterpiece of detail and little help. Every ravine and switchback, not the how. Whisk nudged a confusing swirl of ink. A river, or a grumpy cloud. “Technically correct. Not very helpful.”

A large shadow filled the doorway. Ogre Mallow, moss-coloured, eyes like warm summer pools, a nose that could sniff a moonpetal from miles. “Heard the fuss. Sky Bloom. Smells like damp earth and shy sunshine.”

“Just the ogre we need. The map is more riddle than guide.”

Mallow’s huge hands were careful on the parchment. “The Scholar’s Scrawl. Knows where, not how. The quickest way isn’t always ink. Follow my nose.”

They scrambled steep stony slopes. Air thinner. Wind keener. Iris, wanting to impress, tried a levitation charm across a jagged scree. She hovered unsteadily a few feet up. Whisk yelped, fur bristled.

“Flashy magic,” Mallow said, not unkindly, “often lands you in a prickly patch.” He stepped over the scree with massive feet and offered a steadying hand.

A deep chasm next, a gaping maw. Iris’s brow furrowed. “The map says cross the void with a whisper of wings. My best shimmering flight spell.” Secret words. Glowing patterns. A faint shimmer flickered and died. “Oh, bother.”

Mallow sniffed the edge and pointed with a finger thicker than Iris’s arm. “Strong pines either side. Thick trailing vines. A good strong bridge. Ordinary, perhaps. It will hold.”

His strength, her knots. Whisk scurried first, brave and curious. The vine bridge swayed and felt as solid as mountain.

On a high windswept plateau the sun painted orange and lavender. The map wanted a grove of twisted junipers. “Where the shadow of the solitary peak touches the sleeping stone at twilight. Which shadow? Which stone?”

Mallow inhaled, nose twitching. “That’s not a prophecy. It’s a shopping list with ambition.” He pointed to mossy rocks at the cliff’s edge. “Deepest moss. Wind singing a low lullaby. Shy. Doesn’t like a fuss.”

There, where fading light cast dancing shadows, a single delicate flower: pale luminous blue, pearly edges, a quiet persistent glow. Iris plucked it carefully. The Sky Bloom. No thunderbolt had been required.

In Glimmerbrook she set flower beside Sparkle Stone. No fanfare. Soft luminescence, gentle warmth, the grey remembering how to shimmer. A cheer washed the square. The mayor, tears of relief, clasped her hand. “Your magic. You’ve saved the Frost Festival.”

Iris looked at Whisk grooming with pride, and Mallow’s happy broad face. She did not correct the mayor with a speech. She tucked the map away, the unhelpful swirls and all, and let the stone do the shining. Whisk sneezed stardust that was only dust. The first stars pricked. The Frost Festival, ordinary and bright, could begin.
characters: Iris (witch of the Whispering Peaks), Whisk (an always-alert stoat), Mallow (a gentle ogre)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing mountain adventure fantasy for ages 9-10
author: StoryGen Community
